title: MCP Apps: Primitives, discovery, and the Future of Software - Pietro Zullo, Manufact, Inc
talk_summary: Pietro Zullo of Manufact explains MCP Apps: MCP servers returning sandboxed-iframe UI widgets with bidirectional host communication (set-state, send-message, streaming partial tool args, UI-only vs model-visible outputs), plus how to distribute MCP servers/apps via ChatGPT/Claude/Cursor stores and dynamic discovery. It is primarily a protocol/ecosystem and distribution talk, not an agent-operations talk.

takeaways.technique: Split tool output into UI-only vs model-visible payloads
takeaways.what_they_do: An MCP tool returns multiple typed outputs: rich structured data rendered in a widget, and a separate minimal text/JSON payload sent to the model, so the model never sees private or bulky data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's two types of output, the ones that are shown in the UI, to put it simply, and the ones that are sent to the model

takeaways.technique: Client-capability negotiation before choosing output format
takeaways.what_they_do: The server inspects client metadata to detect whether the host supports widgets; if not, it returns a different (text) output so information isn't lost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you don't show the widget, you need to return a different output because ... some of the information was returning the widget but maybe you want to give it to the model

takeaways.technique: Streaming partial tool arguments to drive incremental work
takeaways.what_they_do: As the model streams tokens into tool arguments, the consumer updates/renders incrementally rather than waiting for the complete call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the model streams the input tokens into the tool arguments, you can ... take those partial input and update the UI incrementally

takeaways.what_they_do: Before submitting an MCP server to ChatGPT/Claude/Cursor stores, they run the same automated checks the stores run (tool annotations, argument schemas, auth, generated screenshots and test prompts).
takeaways.evidence_quote: we check and we try to do all the checks that those clients will do in the submission process
